oracle_backing_diagnosis.scope: Independent original CPU cold/prepared mapping probe; counts excluded from equivalence totals.

repeat_group_diagnosis.finding: Aligned forward REP MOVS/STOS data breakpoints on the recorded E core may be delayed to a 16-byte iteration group; P cores and reverse/TF variants stop per element. This is an architectural fast-string allowance, not a missing trap or an equality to mask. Guest CR0.CD did not change this oracle behavior.
repeat_group_diagnosis.probe_scope: Original bytes only, 1/2/4/8-byte elements, counts 3/17/257, first/second watched element. The callbacks in runtime are explicit target inputs; these samples do not define all processor alignment/page/cache cases.

after.scope: Software event-owner liveness, not an original-CPU equivalence comparison

contract.binding: X86InstructionDebugProfile::Watchpoints requires a bound DR0-3/6/7 bank, zero DEBUGCTL and an explicit target. Existing debug profiles retain their earlier admitted controls. DR6 BLD/RTM remain fixed to one; RTM, BTF, PT and other unbound controls refuse.
contract.matching: The shared owner checks all four enabled slots, linear byte ranges, read/write versus write-only, and protected-mode wrap. Intel length-masked unaligned data ranges are measured behavior, not a portable interpretation of undefined alignment. Execution comparators require LEN=0; I/O requires CR4.DE and 1/2/4-byte lengths.
contract.observation: A borrowed scoped memory observer records completed loads, RMW reads and committed writes. It does not allocate per access, observe instruction fetch or physical page walks, or publish a cause for store preparation. System descriptors, TSS, IDT and event frames participate.
contract.publication: A completed instruction or explicitly bound REP debug group consumes new and retained data causes. RF does not suppress them; TF and next-PC execution comparators combine according to the qualified target. ICEBP retains separate cause rules. Failed instructions discard their speculative data causes without discarding already committed RAM/device effects.
contract.repeat_groups: Watchpoints plus memory REP requires an explicit X86RepeatDebugBinding, including zero counts. The pure EndGroup input sees the completed element and address-width indices/count. MOVS/STOS may retain pending data causes across elements and host budgets/backing stops. TF, other string operations, ports and final completion retain their own boundaries; ordinary accepted faults discard pending causes. The runtime never infers a host CPU model. Aligned forward native cases bind the measured P/E profiles to 1/16-byte boundaries across 1/2/4/8-byte operands, forward/reverse direction, counts and watched positions. Other alignments/targets require their own boundary producer.
contract.stack_shadow: MOV/POP SS postpones data causes in PendingData rather than DR6. A physical backing stop retains them; an ordinary accepted exception drops them. Successful software entry preserves the trap request but reports only the new event-access B bits, so a delayed trap can have B0-3 clear.
contract.legacy_replay: The protected event owner retains completed descriptor/TSS reads and skips completed stores after a backing stop. A partial frame may already have overwritten those inputs. Fault transitions and post-entry data traps clear the access record for the next event while preserving prior RAM effects. Aliased-TSS reference/resume tests cover both 16-bit and 32-bit gates, data causes, one-entry work budgets and changed access-record refusal.
contract.events: Both event owners call one shared cause rule. Accepted-event backing records retain matched completed accesses without replay. SoftwareCompleted remains true if a later data #DB entry faults. Failed entries discard speculative causes before secondary faults or #DF. Watching #DB tables can recurse to shutdown, reported as an endpoint only.
contract.event_work: X86EventDeliveryOptions owns a positive per-call entry-attempt budget (default 4096). A budget stop retains the next event, fault chain, software completion, original acceptance and all committed state/RAM. It is not a CPU exception or shutdown. Fixed-IST recursion, repeated resume, bounded-versus-uninterrupted fault chains, zero-budget and malformed-continuation checks qualify the contract.
contract.oracle_backing: KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY prepares second-level mappings for data-watchpoint comparisons without executing guest code or changing guest page tables. An independent 50,000-run probe reproduced one lost SS-delayed trap on the cold initial run on each P/E core; prepared mappings removed the loss. A fresh-vCPU regression compares full state/RAM on both generated routes. Probe counts are diagnostic and excluded from qualification totals.
contract.ports: The shared port owner reports the actual completed port and width. Only that receipt can create an I/O cause; denied/unavailable/zero-count operations cannot. A later architectural INS fault suppresses #DB while retaining the specified consumed-device/partial-memory progress. Port comparison is zero-extended, without 16-bit wrapping across FFFFh.
contract.selector_fix: Original byte-footprint probes exposed full-slot CS/SS reads in the x64 IRET/RETF source owner. Selectors now read two bytes in both faultable and successful-RAM source paths. Native page-boundary returns verify that unused slot padding need not be mapped.
contract.x64_oracle: Original instruction bytes, KVM guest debugging disabled, independent guest RAM and full represented registers/caches/flags/debug banks/shadows plus all 256 KiB RAM. The main range test covers HighC and LLVM-to-C through Clang and NeverC at O0/O2. Other event, return, REP, continuation and device tests use both C routes at O2.
contract.legacy_oracle: Original protected instructions with independent code/stack/gate widths, CPL0/3 and both legacy/PAE paging. All represented state, debug bank and all 2 MiB RAM are compared. Stack, far transfers, software/fault entries, descriptor/TSS accesses and page walks are included.
contract.matrix: Final fork/r6 SDKs at the recorded source base: complete debug/watchpoint/execution-breakpoint selections on P/E, including legacy event replay; full continuation source and public export suites on P. The earlier complete-* full P paging/paged/source/export runs are retained separately at 6b22e02c55, before integration and explicit REP grouping, and are excluded from these totals. The final selections cover the changed grouping paths and existing debug producers; unrelated full paging cases are not claimed as rerun on the final binary.
contract.counting: CPU comparison totals are summed independently from every original_comparisons test property, including OriginalStackOperandsAndEventTables. The raw launcher field filtered only Watchpoint-named cases and is not the authority for the final sum. Shutdown endpoints, software-only tests and diagnostic probes remain separate.

earlier_full_p_baseline.recheck_scope: The new optional grouping path executes only for Watchpoints with memory REP. Recheck every debug selection on both SDKs and P/E, plus full source/export after merging shared HighC and call changes. Keep full pre-group paging evidence at its real source/product epoch.

diagnostics_excluded_from_totals.finding: The frozen two-SDK P suites passed, but complete-native-debug-e failed REP MOVSB because the E core completed a fast-string group before #DB. The scheduler stopped further jobs. Retained all source/products in pre-repeat-groups, confirmed the architectural group allowance with independent original-byte probes, added explicit runtime grouping and regressions, and qualified grouped-* after integrating dev at the recorded new base. No partial or failed complete-* run is counted in the final totals.

Stopped the intermediate full matrix after an independent host-backing probe confirmed that the protected event owner reread TSS inputs overwritten by its own partial frame and incorrectly shut down. Saved source/products under pre-replay; grouped-* is the final matrix after retaining completed event accesses.

diagnostics_excluded_from_totals.run: pre-liveness and final-* initial full suites
diagnostics_excluded_from_totals.finding: Archived pre-budget source/products and partial full-suite passes are diagnostic only. Fixed-IST recursion could spin indefinitely; the final grouped-* matrix uses resumable event-work bounds.

The test fixture retained its prior one-entry work limit and used a software gate with the wrong DPL. Reset the work configuration and selected a not-present DPL3 gate so the intended NP/DF chain is exercised.

One original CPU run lost an SS-delayed trap on software entry. Independent repeated original-byte probes and per-vCPU KVM counters isolated cold second-level mapping faults. Prepare mappings and retain a fresh-vCPU regression; never mask the differing state or count the earlier failing run as a pass.
Fixed the fixture shadow member spelling and an RMW fault fixture that accidentally unmapped its own TSS; the final fixture faults the intended operand page.

Watching #DB tables recursively shuts the CPU down. These cases moved to a separate explicit original/model shutdown endpoint check; no undefined shutdown register image is counted as full-state equivalence.

Byte 10 of an IRETQ frame triggered the model watchpoint but not the original CPU. Corrected CS/SS reads from whole slots to two-byte selectors, then verified native P/E footprints and page-boundary success before rerunning focused and full suites.
Passing diagnostic/focused checks are retained but excluded from final matrix totals.
The KVM intercepted-port emulator did not deliver matching I/O watchpoints. Kept this as unavailable physical I/O evidence; device-receipt behavior is checked by separate software regressions.

limitations: Data-watchpoint native tests require KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY; absent kernel/header support is an explicit skip. The raw cold-mapping probes are diagnostic only.

The Intel VMX/KVM oracle qualifies the declared nontransactional profile on the recorded P/E cores. Unaligned comparator addresses and delayed software-entry B-bit behavior are explicit measured target choices.
Fast-string debug group selection is a caller-bound target input. The measured 1/16-byte aligned native fixtures do not qualify arbitrary unaligned, page/cache-dependent or other-processor grouping.
I/O watchpoint delivery has software contract tests but no physical-port CPU equivalence qualification through this local emulator. No host physical port access was attempted.
Recursive #DB table-watch tests compare shutdown endpoints only; architectural state after shutdown is not qualified.
The bound KVM CPU does not expose LA57. Each full paging suite skips the one native five-level case; these skips are not passes.

Debug-aware function activation, general i386/compatibility source dispatch, branch/task/transactional debug, real/VM86/task environments, FRED/CET, software SMM and SGX/AEX remain separate incomplete contracts.
LLVM and NeverC native intrinsic APIs are unchanged by this runtime milestone. No LLVM release, production SDK pin change or LLVM gitlink update is claimed.
